text:
Joel Farabee is playing the most minutes of his career, 19:06 a night, and Calgary is getting a return: 17 points in 19 games, nine of them on the power play, and six goals in his last ten. He ended a breakaway drought in the Nov. 8 overtime comeback against the Flyers, his old team, and scored shorthanded in the same game, which is the sort of night that tells you how much the Flames are asking of him.

How much of it holds? His shooting, 13.7%, is right around league average, so the goals aren't a fluke. His point rate is the part to doubt: our talent range sits well below his current pace, and his team has scored 4.8 more goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice. That kind of on-ice luck usually fades.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 61% of his shots coming off the rush last season. Watch how often Calgary gets out of its own end with him on; that's where his game starts.
headline: Farabee has found a home in Calgary
